answer.rationale: memory_c2 directly evidences the low-cost vendor path: sharp unit-cost reduction, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing. memory_c6 checks whether a multi-year term with the incumbent could have met the 18% mandate via volume pricing, which would let me compare the two cost levers. The incumbent has already refused to reopen price (memory_c4's renegotiation channel is exhausted this cycle), so renew_incumbent cannot hit the 18% target. negotiate_terms is effectively foreclosed by that refusal. defer_decision leaves the 14-day expiry unresolved with no auto-renew, creating acute delivery risk at 94% line utilization. add_second_source is prudent (memory_c3) but does not by itself satisfy the cost mandate and consumes the single decision slot. Switching primary supply to the vendor whose quote already meets the mandate alone satisfies the finance requirement while memory_c2 confirms low transition risk. Residual delivery risk at 94% utilization is the main watch-item; I will flag for next review whether a second-source backstop should be the first action in the following cycle.
